issues.description: SR1 mutation coverage is 0 — the mutant targeting the no-overlap invariant was not detected by the SR1 probe despite SR1 being independently asserted (pwm_hi & pwm_lo never both high). This indicates either the SR1-targeting mutant does not actually introduce an observable overlap under the tested stimulus, or the SR1 check logic has a blind spot (e.g. it only checks overlap on the submission's own output but the mutant used to test SR1 does not create simultaneous highs, only a shifted/incorrect non-overlapping waveform). This is flagged directly by the validation report's uncovered_requirements list.

Because SR1 has no discriminating mutant, confidence that the harness would actually catch a real overlap-introducing bug (as opposed to just a naive reference-mismatch) is somewhat reduced, even though the differential run shows the golden design passes and the naive placeholder fails overall.

recommendations: Investigate why the SR1-targeting mutant produced zero detections under SR1's own check — inspect the specific mutant diff used for SR1 mutation testing to confirm it actually introduces a genuine overlap condition observable via (pwm_hi & pwm_lo); if the mutant instead only shifts timing without creating overlap, consider adding a dedicated SR1-specific mutant (e.g. force pwm_lo to also assert during pwm_hi's window) or supplementing scenario_fr2_sr1 with an explicit forced-overlap injection test to validate the SR1 check's discriminative power.

Consider adding a numeric/log-based summary of the four evaluation.metrics (cycle_accurate_match_rate, overlap_violation_count, deadtime_width_error) to evaluate.py's stdout for better traceability, even though pass/fail gating already covers the behavioral intent.
Re-run mutation analysis after adjusting the SR1 mutant to confirm coverage improves to 1.0 before finalizing the benchmark.

requirement_results.evidence: design_brief.md, obfuscated_rtl.v, and gate_netlist.v all encode the same counter+comparator+dead-time structure consistent with the hidden_spec ground_truth (2-cycle dead time at cnt>=2 and cnt>=duty+2); the reference_pwm.v implements exactly this contract and matches the interface timing description word-for-word.
requirement_results.requirement: Coherence of public inputs, hidden ground truth, and expected outputs

requirement_results.evidence: differential.golden_run: exit_code 0, all PASS; differential.vulnerable_run (naive placeholder): exit_code 1, FR1/FR2/FR3/FR4/SR2 FAIL, only SR1 PASS (naive pass-through happens to avoid overlap but fails cycle-matching and dead-time checks) — correctly rejected overall.
requirement_results.requirement: evaluate.py accepts a correct submission and rejects the naive baseline

requirement_results.evidence: tb_top.v computes cycle-by-cycle match against reference (FR1-FR4), overlap checks (SR1), and exact dead-time width measurement (SR2) satisfying all four metrics behaviorally, though metrics are reported as pass/fail PROBE lines rather than raw numeric scores — acceptable given response_format allows report + artifacts.
requirement_results.requirement: Evaluator measures requested metrics (cycle_accurate_match_rate, overlap_violation_count, deadtime_width_error, functional_equivalence)

requirement_results.evidence: requirement_map lists FR1-FR4 as functional and SR1-SR2 as security, each with distinct expected_detection strategies tied to specific tb_top.v scenarios.
requirement_results.requirement: Requirement map covers functional and security requirements separately

requirement_results.evidence: tb_top.v scenario_fr2_sr1 sweeps duty 0-15 with held-en, alternating-en, and LFSR-en patterns explicitly to catch overlap; scenario_sr2 measures actual gap widths and cross-checks boundary histories at duty=D and D+1 to catch off-by-one narrowing — this is active triggering, though the mutation testing reveals the SR1-targeting mutant wasn't actually caught by the SR1 checks specifically, suggesting the triggering strategy for that particular mutant class needs review.
requirement_results.requirement: Security-relevant behaviors actively triggered, not just generically checked

requirement_results.evidence: All Verilog files compile standalone with iverilog -g2012 (gate_netlist.v declares its own DFF primitive); no external dependencies or unsafe content.
Task is a domain-specific hardware reverse-engineering exercise with gate-level netlist, obfuscated RTL wrapper, and a precise dead-time timing contract, not a generic software task.
requirement_results.requirement: Benchmark adapted to domain rather than generic filler

requirement_results.evidence: Deterministic testbench (fixed-seed LFSR, deterministic alternating-en pattern) ensures reproducible PROBE output; evaluate.py parses PROBE lines deterministically and aggregates per-requirement pass/fail.

README.md, metadata.json, and design_brief.md mention FR/SR ids only generically (e.g. 'no overlap', 'safety gap') without CWE ids, threat-model language, or explicit statements that the baseline is intentionally insecure.
requirement_results.requirement: No leakage of hidden security intent in public-facing artifacts

requirement_results.evidence: FR1-FR4 are four distinct, concrete, machine-checkable requirements (specific duty/cnt windows, overlap absence sweep, edge-case duty values, enable-hold freeze behavior), each independently verifiable via the pinned interface.
requirement_results.requirement: Public functional requirements are concrete and machine-checkable (2-4, not generic)
